contentBlocks.body: Production systems need evidence. Structured logs keep important fields queryable, while metrics show rates, latency, and failures over time. A strong .NET answer mentions correlation ids, user-safe fields, and avoiding secrets in logs.

contentBlocks.body: Do not log access tokens, passwords, raw authorization headers, or sensitive personal data.

A log call takes a message template, not a finished string. `ILogger` binds the arguments to the `{Placeholders}` by position and stores each one as a property, which is what makes `LessonId = 'l-42'` searchable. String interpolation (`$"Completed {lessonId}"`) formats the text before the logger sees it, so the properties are gone. `{@Review}` asks the provider to destructure an object into fields. Anything sensitive must be redacted before it is written, because logs are copied to many places and kept for a long time.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Why prefer structured logging over one large interpolated string?

choices: Fields like LessonId and UserId remain queryable
It makes logs impossible to read

knowledgeItems.prompt: Which metric instrument fits request latency?

payload.explanation: A histogram records a distribution, so you can chart p50, p95 and p99. A counter only tells you how many times something happened.
